name: שָׁאוּל
summary: Above all Saul son of Kish, of Benjamin, the first king of Israel, anointed by Samuel and rejected for not keeping Yahweh's word; he fell on his sword on Gilboa (1Sa 9–31). Others bear the name: a king of Edom (Gen 36:37), a son of Simeon, father of the clan of the Shaulite (Gen 46:10; Num 26:13), and a Levite of Kohath (1Ch 6:9). Saul of Tarsus, also of Benjamin, bore the same name: the voice called him Σαούλ, the Hebrew form, and Luke says “Saul, who is also Paul” (Act 9:4; 13:9). The name is the passive participle of שָׁאַל, “asked”, the form scripture uses for what is asked of Yahweh and given (1Sa 1:28). It suits the king: Israel “asked for” a king, and Samuel says of Saul, “here is the king … whom you asked for (שְׁאֶלְתֶּם)” (1Sa 12:13), and Paul, “they asked for a king, and God gave them Saul” (Act 13:21). Scripture does not say that was why he was so named.

evidence.note: Kish “had a son, and his name was שָׁאוּל, a choice young man and good”, taller than all the people.
The form the name is: Samuel “is שָׁאוּל to Yahweh”, granted, the one asked for and given.
The same participle, “borrowed”: “Alas, my lord, and it was borrowed (וְהוּא שָׁאוּל).”
“The people who were asking a king from him (הַשֹּׁאֲלִים מֵאִתּוֹ מֶלֶךְ).”
“Here is the king whom you have chosen, whom you asked for (אֲשֶׁר שְׁאֶלְתֶּם).”
Saul son of Kish taken by lot from the tribe of Benjamin.
Samuel anoints him “ruler over his inheritance”.
“Now your kingdom shall not stand; Yahweh has sought for himself a man after his heart.”
“Because you have rejected the word of Yahweh, he has rejected you from being king.”
Saul took the sword and fell on it; Saul, his three sons and his armour-bearer died together.
He died for his trespass and for asking of the אוֹב, and did not seek Yahweh; so the kingdom was turned to David.
“They asked for (ᾐτήσαντο) a king, and God gave them Saul (Σαοὺλ) son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, forty years”; the Peshitta, שֵאלו … לשָאוָל.
Shaul of Rehoboth by the River, king in Edom.
Shaul, son of Simeon by a Canaanite woman.
“Of Shaul, the clan of the Shaulite (הַשָּׁאוּלִי).”
Shaul, a Levite of the line of Kohath.
The witnesses laid their garments at the feet of a young man called Saul (Σαύλου).
“Σαοὺλ Σαούλ, why are you persecuting me?”: the Hebrew name, undeclined; the Peshitta, שָאוָל שָאוָל.
“Saul, who is also Paul (Σαῦλος δὲ ὁ καὶ Παῦλος)”.
Paul: “of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews”, the tribe of the king whose name he bore.

note: Takes v.ag.ac (the name; its count is by spelling and takes in tokens of the verb) and the gentilic שָׁאוּלִי (v.ag.ad, Num 26:13), which TIPNR lists as a group form of Shaul@Gen.46.10. People: all four TIPNR records spelled שָׁאוּל, and Paul@Act.7.58, whose TIPNR summary gives Saul (Σαούλ, Σαῦλος) among his names; review whether Paul's record should be tagged here, since it will also put this entry on Greek words naming him Παῦλος. The Septuagint and the New Testament write Σαούλ, and Acts also the Greek-declined Σαῦλος. The reading “asked (for)” rests on the form (the qal passive participle, as 1Sa 1:28 and 2Ki 6:5); scripture never explains the name, and the link to Israel's asking for a king is the reader's, not the text's: 1Sa 1:20–28 plays on the same participle for Samuel.
